newsitem.title: ITALY: Consob wants answers on Olivetti accounts.
newsitem.headline: Consob wants answers on Olivetti accounts.

text.p: Italy's stock exchange watchdog Consob has given troubled high-tech group Olivetti 24 hours to reply to seven queries on its first-half 1996 figures, a Consob official said.
The official said Olivetti shares would not be suspended and trading would resume on Tuesday morning.
Olivetti shares collapsed on the bourse today after a two-day suspension, forcing exchange authorities to step in again and halt trading until tomorrow.

Consob officials carried out a preliminary examination of Olivetti's six-month figures this morning and intend to call in Olivetti managers this week and consult the group's auditors next week. No details of the queries were given.
Olivetti surprised the stock market last Tuesday when it announced a first-half loss of 440.8 billion lire and said its chairman of 18 years, Carlo De Benedetti, was stepping down.

Consob said on Friday night after Olivetti issued a statement defending its accounting practices and saying its figures for the first six months were in order that the bourse watchdog would continue its investigation of Olivetti's accounts.

Consob said then it had not made a full and detailed examination of Olivetti's first-half figures but had made sure the company's statement contained enough information to allow its shares to resume trading today after a two day suspension last week.
